From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API questions: residency + deletion (Prism security questionnaire)

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the questionnaire. Below is a focused response to each of the three items you raised. I’m attaching our operational playbook and a short KMS integration summary for your auditors. If you want, we can also provide audit extracts for a test tenant after you sign an NDA for live data.

1) Storage locations and service tiers
- Hosted API primary storage: customer request payloads, prompts, and generated outputs are persisted in encrypted object storage (us-west-2 by default for US tenants).
- Regional options: customers can request alternate regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1) at provisioning; region selection is enforced at the tenant routing layer and persists across the runtime and long-term storage.
- Service tiers:
  * Standard (multi-tenant hosted): data-at-rest encrypted with customer-managed keys (optional) or Redwood-managed keys; default retention windows apply.
  * Dedicated: isolated tenancy with dedicated GPU pool; same retention model but physical separation.

2) Deletion lifecycle (customer erasure request) — operational summary
- Step A — Soft-delete (0): immediate application-layer mark for deletion. In the primary object store the object is tombstoned within seconds; TTL metadata updated.
- Step B — Logical purge (T+1 to T+7 days): accounting and indexes are cleaned up, caches and in-memory prefix/KV caches are invalidated within 1–24 hours depending on active sessions.
- Step C — Physical purge from primary store (T+7 to T+30 days): objects are permanently deleted from the active bucket and S3 lifecycle transitions are prevented from restoring them; deletion manifests are recorded.
- Step D — Backup snapshot purge (T+30 to T+180 days): snapshots and long-term backups are on a snapshot cycle; we remove references and rewrite retention manifests such that the next backup sweep expunges any remaining data. Full irrevocable removal from cold archives completes within 180 days in the worst case; typical completion is 45–90 days depending on backup schedule and customer options.
- Edge cases:
  * Replicated region deletion: when a tenant is geo-replicated we issue coordinated deletion across regions using the same timeline.
  * Legal hold / eDiscovery flags: if a valid legal hold is in place, deletion is paused and the request is escalated to legal/compliance.

3) Audit evidence we can provide
- Deletion manifests: time-stamped records of tombstones, logical purges, and final object deletion events.
- S3 object-level lifecycle logs (purge records) and object deletion markers.
- KMS key-rotation & key-deletion logs when customer-managed keys are used.
- Access logs and operational runbook snippets (who executed the workflow, job ids).
- Optional: a signed attestation of deletion from Redwood operations (DocuSign), available for enterprise customers under contract.

Attachments included: redwood_deletion_playbook_v1.2.pdf, kms-integration-summary.txt, s3-backup-retention-matrix.csv

If you want more granular timestamps (e.g., an object-level audit extract for a sample customer), tell me the auditor email and we’ll generate a scrubbed extract.

Best,

Also: we require an example deletion manifest showing the fields that will be present (object id, tombstone time, final deletion time, initiator, job id). A redacted sample would be fine.

Thanks — if easier, you can share the sample manifest in the Drive link you provided.

Elena

Subject: Re: Hosted API questions: residency + deletion (Prism security questionnaire)

Elena —

Great questions. Quick answers and next steps:

- Tombstone retention: tombstone records (deletion manifests) are retained in our event store for 365 days by default (configurable for enterprise plans). Tombstones include a cryptographic hash of the object id, the deletion initiator, and the job id. They are not reversible to plaintext content once the object has been physically purged.

- Backup worst-case recoverability: the 180-day worst-case applies only to cold-archive snapshots that are immutable for compliance buckets (customers can opt for shorter retention). Standard backup tiers (hot/warm snapshots) typically purge within 45–90 days. We will provide exact retention policy text you can paste into the questionnaire: 

  "Redwood retention summary: primary-store physical purge: 7-30 days; warm backup removal: 45-90 days; cold-archive removal: up to 180 days (default), configurable per-customer. All deletion events are recorded in deletion manifests and immutable audit logs."

- Sample deletion manifest: I’ve uploaded a redacted example to the shared drive (link below) and attached a CSV extract (s3-backup-retention-matrix.csv) showing fields you can map to your controls. The manifest includes: object_hash, tenant_id (redacted), tombstone_time, logical_purge_time, final_deletion_time, initiator (operator/service), job_id, region, retention_class.

Next steps: Evelyn on our ops team will generate a scrubbed audit extract for a non-production tenant and provide JSON/CSV samples for your auditors. Evelyn — can you pick a convenient time today to push the file to the Drive link and we’ll send DocuSign attestation language if Prism needs it?

Cheers,
Michael Grant
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
